problem: Removing the time-went-backwards guard from _observe lets out-of-order timestamps in: a call with a later now permanently evicts entries still inside the window at the true time, so limit(1,10) allows allow(100), remaining(200), allow(105), and out-of-order appends leave the deque unsorted so expired entries behind newer ones are never evicted, silently turning a ValueError into a rate-limit bypass or wrongful denial.

retry_after treats q[0] as the oldest entry, which no longer holds once out-of-order timestamps are appended, so limit(2,10) after allow(100), allow(95) reports retry_after(100) == 10.0 instead of 5.0.
With the guard gone, _last_now is written by _observe but never read, leaving dead state that implies time ordering is still enforced.

Pre-existing and not introduced by this diff: now is never checked to be finite, so allow(key, nan) or allow(key, inf) inserts an entry that never expires and locks the key out permanently without an error.
